[Instruction]
Please act as an impartial judge and evaluate the quality of the response provided by an AI assistant to the user question given the provided document and a reference answer.

Your evaluation should assess the faithfulness, appropriateness, and completeness. Your evaluation should focus on the assistant's answer to the question of the current turn.  You will be given the assistant's answer and a reference answer. You will also be given the user questions and assistant's answers of the previous turns of the conversation. You should consider how well the assistant's answer captures the key information, knowledge points mentioned in the reference answer, and how it respects or builds upon the focus and knowledge points from the previous turns. 

[Faithfulness]: You are given the full conversation, the question of the current turn, the assistant's answer, and documents. You should evaluate how faithful is the assistant's answer to the information in the document and previous conversation.
[Appropriateness]: You should evaluate if the assistant's answer is relevant to the question of the current turn and if it addresses all the issues raised by the question without adding extra information.
[Completeness]: You should evaluate whether the assistant's answer is complete with information from the documents.

Begin your evaluation by comparing the assistant's answer against the reference answer in this turn. Be as objective as possible, and provide a detailed justification for your rating. After providing your explanation, you must rate the response on a scale of 1 to 10, strictly following this format: "Rating: [[rating]]", for example: "Rating: [[5]]".

[The Start of Previous Conversation]
user: How much is the fee to get a copy of the oral argument recording from the court?
assistant: I do not have that information. 
user: Can anyone pay a fee to get a copy of an oral argument recording from the court?
assistant: Yes. Any party may pay a fee to get a copy of their oral argument recording from the court.

user: When you say "any party," it refers to the individuals involved in the case, not the general public, correct?
assistant: Yes, that's correct. In the courts, the individuals or entities directly involved in the case are referred to as parties; for example, ask for the name of party.
user: Who makes the oral arguments?
assistant: To be eligible for an oral argument, a party must have filed a brief that has been accepted by the Court of Appeal. If the respondent did not file a brief, they cannot make an oral argument. If a party is represented by a lawyer, the lawyer will present the oral argument. A party is not required to attend court for the oral argument if they have legal representation. The court will provide all parties with at least 20 days' advance notice, which will include the date, time, and location of the oral argument.
user: Can I decline to participate in an oral argument?
assistant: Yes. You have the option to decline to participate in an oral argument. If you decide not to make an oral argument, it will not affect the court's view of your arguments in the appeal. Not all parties are required to participate in the same way; if only one party wishes to present an oral argument, the court will hold the oral argument for the case but will not compel the other parties to participate. 
Many appeals do not include oral arguments because all parties choose to waive (give up) their right to do so. When there is no oral argument, the Court of Appeal justices decide based solely on the written briefs and the appeal record. It is important to note that oral arguments do not speed up or delay the appeal process.
user: Good to know. 
assistant: Is there anything else I can help you with?
[The End of Previous Conversation]

[The Start of Current Turn Question]
Can I have the fees waived?
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
If you wish to request a waiver for the $390 filing fee in the Court of Appeal, you must submit a Request to Waive Court Fees form (FW-001) along with your first filing in the Court of Appeal. Submitting this fee waiver form with your initial filing means you will only have to pay fees once the court decides on your fee waiver application. 
You can fill out the Request to Waive Court Fees form (FW-001) online. 
During an appeal, fees are associated with both the trial court and the Court of Appeal. If you are the appellant and wish to have your court fees waived, you must secure a fee waiver from both courts. 
To have fees waived in both courts, you need to complete two fee waiver forms (FW-001)—one for the trial court and one for the Court of Appeal. You should submit both forms to the trial court when you file your notice of appeal. If you already have a fee waiver from the trial court, it may still be valid when you file your notice of appeal. 
Fee waivers expire 60 days after the trial court's judgment. You may qualify for a fee waiver if your household income (before taxes) is less than the amounts specified in item 5b of form FW-001 and if the court determines that you do not have sufficient income to cover basic household needs and court fees.
[The End of Reference Answer]

[The Start of Assistant's Answer]
You can request a court-fee waiver using Form FW-001, but the provided documents do not establish whether the fee for a copy of an oral argument recording can be waived or whether you qualify. [S2] [S4] If you need fees waived in both the trial court and the Court of Appeal, you must obtain a waiver in each court; neither court can waive the other court’s fees. [S3]
[The End of Assistant's Answer]

[The Start of Document]
Fill out form APP-008


 Request to Waive Court Fees, Form FW-001 (Optional for Appellant and Respondent) During an appeal there are fees in both the trial court and the Court of Appeal.

If you want to have fees waived in both courts, you must have a fee waiver in both courts. That’s because a trial court cannot waive fees in the Court of Appeal, and the Court of Appeal cannot waive fees in the trial court.

Fill out a Request to Waive Court Fees form FW-001 online
Learn more about how to qualify and what fees can be waived
Watch a video or read instructions about how to fill out the fee waiver form


 Please check with your trial court and ask if you need to submit a new fee waiver application.

Learn more about how to qualify and what fees can be waived
Read the California Court’s information sheet on fee waivers


Get instructions for how to fill out the fee waiver form FW-001


 What happens if I don’t pay the notice of appeal filing fees? If you do not pay the filing fees or if your check bounces, the Court of Appeal will send a notice that you have 15 days to pay the fees or have them waived.

Additional Filings – California Appellate Courts
If you already have a fee waiver from the trial court, it could still be valid when you file your notice of appeal. Fee waivers expire 60 days after the trial court’s judgment. Please check with your trial court and ask if you need to submit a new fee waiver application.

If you do not have a fee waiver from the trial court or your fee waiver is expired, you must complete a fee waiver form FW-001 for the trial court.

Remember that you must complete a separate fee waiver form FW-001 for the Court of Appeal and file it at the trial court when you file your notice of appeal.

 I am a Respondent If you want your court fees to be waived in both the trial court and the Court of Appeal, you must have a fee waiver in both courts.

Be sure to specify the name of the court you are applying to on the fee waiver form.
[The End of Document]
